references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, specific creeping things that are unclean are listed, including those that go on their belly or on four legs.
The following verse gives the reason for the prohibition: The people of Israel shall not make themselves unclean with creeping things, because the Lord is holy.
Concerns insects with wings that walk on four legs and provides an exception for those that have jumping legs—related to criteria for creeping things.
Repeats the prohibition against eating winged creeping things, as they are unclean for the Israelites.
The serpent was cursed to crawl on its belly (גָּחוֹן), the same word used in Leviticus 11:42 about animals that go on their belly.
Isaiah prophesies judgment against those who eat unclean things, including abominations (שֶׁקֶץ), using the same terminology as in Leviticus.
Peter's vision included four-legged animals and creeping things (ἑρπετά), where God declared them clean—a New Testament fulfillment of the purity law.
Peter describes the content of the vision, including creeping things on the earth, which relates to the categories in Leviticus 11.
